LESSON: WRITING 10.5.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING: PACKING AND SHOPPING LISTS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.5: Writing 10.5.1 Functional Writing: Packing and Shopping lists
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 10.5.1 Functional Writing: Packing and Shopping lists, part of Strand 10 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: What should one consider when grouping items in a packing list? 2. Why should a shopping list be prepared?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify ways of grouping items in packing and shopping lists,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 10.5.1 Functional Writing: Packing and Shopping lists in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. write a packing list for a specified event,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 10.5.1 Functional Writing: Packing and Shopping lists in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. prepare a shopping list for use in a given context,  Search online and offline for samples of packing and shopping lists. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use an appropriate functional part of the body or use appropriate assistive devices to perform this task.  Discuss different ways of grouping items in packing and shopping lists,  Give in pairs the prices of different items in the shopping list to match a given budget. 3. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 10.5.1 Functional Writing: Packing and Shopping lists together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
 Critical thinking is enhanced as learners categorise the various items included in a shopping and packing list in order of

importance.

 Learning to learn is enhanced as prepare and shares a packing list with peers.

103

Values:
 Integrity – as learners come up with shopping lists that adhere to given budgets

 Social responsibility – mastery of writing of shopping and packing list would ensure public projects are completed within

stated budgets.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Financial literacy is enhanced as the learner prepares a realistic budget for the shopping list and categorises items.

Link to other subjects:

Preparing a shopping list involves budgeting which is a concept learnt in Pre-Technical Studies.
